definitions.definition: A deep similarity between two different things where their parts and rules match up in a way that preserves structure.
definitions.example: Like how a map of a subway system and the actual subway tunnels have the same layout even though one is paper and the other is underground.

definitions.definition: The invisible pull that every object with mass has on every other object with mass, like how Earth pulls you down.
definitions.example: When you jump, gravity pulls you back to the ground.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or decay in moral behavior, like how things tend to get worse over time without effort.
definitions.example: A room gets messy on its own (entropy), and a person's good habits can decay without effort (moral entropy).

definitions.definition: A rule where a force gets weaker by the square of the distance, so if you double the distance, the force is four times weaker.
definitions.example: If you move twice as far from a light bulb, it looks only a quarter as bright.

definitions.definition: The energy needed to pull something apart, like the energy required to lift a rocket off Earth.
definitions.example: You need a lot of energy to break a strong magnet off a fridge; that's like binding energy.

definitions.definition: The speed something needs to break free from gravity, like a rocket needs to go 11 km/s to leave Earth.
definitions.example: A ball thrown up comes back down, but if you threw it super fast (escape velocity), it would leave Earth forever.

definitions.definition: An action that exactly reverses or undoes the structure of a previous event.
definitions.example: If someone pushes a door closed, the counter-move is pushing it open the same way.

definitions.definition: A rule that works both ways, so each side limits or affects the other.
definitions.example: A seesaw: if one side goes up, the other must go down, and vice versa.

definitions.definition: The first hint of the gospel in the Bible, found in Genesis 3:15, where God promises a savior.
definitions.example: It's like a trailer for a movie that shows the hero will defeat the villain.

definitions.definition: A way of reading the Bible where people or events in the Old Testament are seen as patterns for Jesus in the New Testament.
definitions.example: Adam is a 'type' of Jesus because both are key figures for humanity.

definitions.definition: The study of sin, what it is and how it works.
definitions.example: Like biology is the study of life, hamartiology is the study of sin.

definitions.definition: Beings that can make choices between right and wrong, like humans.
definitions.example: A rock is not a moral agent because it can't choose, but you are because you can decide to help or hurt.

definitions.definition: God's free and undeserved help or love given to people.
definitions.example: If you break a rule but your parent forgives you anyway, that's like grace.

definitions.definition: A way of matching parts of one system to parts of another so that their relationships stay the same.
definitions.example: Matching the keys on a piano to the notes on a sheet of music so each key plays the right note.

definitions.definition: A general similarity or connection between two things, but not as strong as an isomorphism.
definitions.example: A map and the real landscape correspond, but the map is not exactly the same.

definitions.definition: A perfect one-to-one matching where every item in one set pairs with exactly one in the other, and nothing is left out.
definitions.example: If you have 5 apples and 5 baskets, a bijective map puts one apple in each basket with none left over.

definitions.definition: Specific conditions that, if met, would prove a theory wrong.
definitions.example: If you claim all swans are white, seeing one black swan is a falsification criterion.

definitions.definition: Information that comes from observation or experiments, not just theory.
definitions.example: If you test a medicine and see it works, that's empirical evidence.

definitions.definition: A sudden change that happens when a certain level is reached, like water boiling at 100°C.
definitions.example: You push a door slowly, and it doesn't open until you push hard enough to cross a threshold.

definitions.definition: A change from one state to another, like ice melting into water.
definitions.example: When you heat ice, it suddenly turns to water at 0°C — that's a phase transition.

definitions.definition: A break or jump in a pattern, not a smooth change.
definitions.example: If you graph a step, it jumps up suddenly instead of sloping — that's a discontinuity.

definitions.definition: A Greek word (pronounced KSOO-lon) meaning 'wood' or 'tree,' used in the Bible for the cross.
definitions.example: In Acts 5:30, 'tree' is xulon, referring to the cross Jesus died on.
